title: No silent films; appearing in Rhythm on the River
summary: He never played for silent movies; his film credit is Rhythm on the River with Bing Crosby and Wingy Manone.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I gave it up. I had to quit. Yeah. What about playing a silent movie? What would that be like? Would you have to read much to do that? Oh. What a new movie would come up like? How would you play it? How did you know what to do?

Well, I never did play silent. Oh, you never did? No. I never did. I played... The only thing I played... around 1936 when I... first movie I made with Bing Crosby, rhythm on the river. You know, where they can see you and they can hear you play.
Oh, you were in that? With Wingy? Yeah.
Yeah, I got the picture. I've never seen it.
No. I've heard the record, you know, that Wingy.

What's the name of the movie? Uh, uh, Rhythm on the River. It's a good tune. It's a good tune, sure. Uh, Larry Crosby was supposed to send me the music and I never did get it, so... I might have it. Yeah? Call me when I get back to work. Yeah. And I'll look it up right there for you. Yeah, all right.
I've got it by Wingy. And I... You did, yeah. You know the record? I think it's on the back of I think, well, ain't it a shame about name or something like that, you know?
